findings.title: Silence action is a no-op for Prometheus-only list items
findings.body: GrafanaRuleListItem now passes only promRule, and the menu can expose Silence notifications using its Prometheus abilities. Clicking it only sets showSilenceDrawer, while the drawer at lines 104–105 still requires a Grafana ruler rule and receives that rule. Consequently, clicking Silence notifications in the new Grafana rule list does nothing. Load the ruler rule on demand or adapt the drawer to the Prometheus rule before exposing this action.

findings.title: Prometheus abilities do not restore Delete and Pause menu actions
findings.body: The new list supplies promRule without rulerRule, but the Pause menu item still requires rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) at line 123 and Delete still requires rulerRule at line 165. Thus both actions disappear from every Grafana rule in the new list even for users with the appropriate permissions, despite calculating their Prometheus abilities. These actions need Prometheus-compatible handlers or on-demand ruler loading rather than retaining the ruler-only rendering guards.

findings.title: skipToken still grants Grafana duplicate abilities
findings.body: Passing skipToken substitutes undefined but does not disable the returned abilities. With no rule, loading is false and duplicateSupported becomes true, so Duplicate is allowed whenever the user has Grafana rule-create permission. AlertRuleMenu calls this hook with skipToken for every data-source rule and ORs its result with the ruler ability. This can expose Duplicate for external rules whose ruler API does not support it, or plugin-provided external rules for which duplication was explicitly disabled. A skipped rule should return unsupported abilities rather than global Grafana abilities.

findings.title: Combined-rule abilities lose the federated-group immutability check
findings.body: useAllAlertRuleAbilities previously checked isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group), but now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which hardcodes isFederated to false. Existing consumers of the combined-rule hook therefore treat federated Mimir rules as mutable and expose Update and Delete when the user has external write permission, whereas these operations were deliberately unsupported for federated groups. Preserve the group-level federation check when adapting the combined-rule hook.
